newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended lower on Wednesday after profit taking emerged as dealers' expectations of a rate cut diminished following neutral December CPI data and a weaker peseta.
"The market at the end of the day came to the conclusion that the Bank of Spain will not cut its official rate tomorrow," said Valentin Fernandez, economist at Credit Lyonnais.
But he added that the Spanish market remained strong.
"The spread (10-yr over Bunds) widened to 98 bps, but soon it bounced back. We also saw buying interest when March futures dipped below 114," Fernandez said.
Earlier this morning, the 10-year spread over Bunds hit a record low at 90 bps.
Though the yield curve remained largely unchanged from Tuesday, dealers said it could flatten a little on Thursday if the Bank of Spain left its key money market rate unchanged at 6.25 percent.
"But later this week, the yield curve will pick up again, starting to steepen further," a dealer said.
